numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Stop coordinate descent when the duality gap satisfies the tolerance inclusively: use `gap <= tol` (instead of stopping only when `gap < tol`), and similarly stop when the biggest coordinate update ratio satisfies `d_w_max / w_max <= d_w_tol` (instead of `<`).
trigger_conditions: When `gap` equals the tolerance boundary (`gap == tol`) inside `enet_coordinate_descent_gram`, the behavior should stop (because the condition changed from `gap < tol` to `gap <= tol`).

When the biggest coordinate update ratio equals the tolerance ratio boundary (`d_w_max / w_max == d_w_tol`) in `enet_coordinate_descent_gram`, the behavior should stop (because the condition changed from `d_w_max / w_max < d_w_tol` to `d_w_max / w_max <= d_w_tol`).
When the code reaches the dual-gap stopping check after the biggest-coordinate-update tolerance condition is met (the comment says it checks the duality gap as the ultimate stopping criterion).
When `n_iter == max_iter - 1`, the code stops regardless (this is one of the conditions shown in the Cython snippet).
oracle_clues: In `sklearn/linear_model/_cd_fast.pyx`, the stopping condition changed from `if gap < tol:` to `if gap <= tol:`.

In `sklearn/linear_model/_cd_fast.pyx` (function `enet_coordinate_descent_gram`), the biggest-coordinate-update ratio condition changed from `d_w_max / w_max < d_w_tol` to `d_w_max / w_max <= d_w_tol`.

In `sklearn/linear_model/_coordinate_descent.py`, the `tol` docstrings for `MultiTaskElasticNet`, `MultiTaskLasso`, and `MultiTaskElasticNetCV` changed from “smaller than tol” to “smaller or equal to tol” for both the coordinate updates and the dual gap stopping description.
PR #31906 body states: the main-branch criterion reads `gap < tol`, but a better version is `gap <= tol`.
Commit message: “tol <= gap instead of tol < gap”.

category_specific_evidence: Main-branch stopping criterion reads `gap < tol`, but better version is `gap <= tol` (PR body: "The stopping criterion in the main branch reads: `gap < tol`, but a better version is `gap <= tol`." / "ENH/FIX stopping criterion for coordinate descent `gap <= tol`").

In coordinate descent docs, the stopping criterion is described with strict inequality changed to non-strict: maximum coordinate update must satisfy `max_j |w_j^{new} - w_j^{old}| is smaller or equal to tol times max_j |w_j|` and dual gap must be `smaller or equal to tol times ||y||_2^2 / n_samples` (discussion patch shows change from `smaller than` to `smaller or equal to` for both updates and dual gap).
In Cython coordinate descent implementation, the stopping check changed from `d_w_max / w_max < d_w_tol` to `d_w_max / w_max <= d_w_tol` (diff:sklearn/linear_model/_cd_fast.pyx).

`tol` docstring changed from "continues until it is smaller than tol" to "continues until it is smaller or equal to tol" for coordinate descent in both `MultiTaskLasso` and `MultiTaskElasticNet` / `MultiTaskElasticNetCV` (diffs in `_coordinate_descent.py`).

Stopping continues until duality gap is smaller (or equal) to the tolerance once the coordinate-update tolerance condition is met (docstrings and `_cd_fast.pyx` comment: "check the duality gap as ultimate stopping criterion").

Test suite changes include suppressing convergence warnings ("Reduce (or explicitly suppress) many Convergence warnings in test suite") but no specific numeric iteration stopping behavior is shown in the provided test snippet.
reproduction_risks: Reproduction may fail to trigger the behavioral difference if it does not hit the boundary case where the relevant inequality changes from strict (`< tol`) to non-strict (`<= tol`), because the fix is specifically about equality handling.

Behavior may depend on whether the implementation reaches the dual gap check (i.e., the tolerance condition for the maximum coordinate update must be satisfied, and then the dual gap stopping check is applied).

Iteration-count boundary is explicitly referenced in the low-level check as `n_iter == max_iter - 1`; reproductions should ensure the run is at or near this limit if the bug manifests there (as suggested by the conditional structure).

Warm-start can alter initialization and therefore affect whether the stopping criterion is evaluated under the equality boundary (relevant because docstrings mention `warm_start`, though the passages do not state any initialization details).

provenance.value: Stop the coordinate-descent optimization when the duality gap reaches the tolerance inclusive (i.e., use `gap <= tol` / stop when `gap` is smaller than or equal to `tol`, rather than strictly smaller `gap < tol`).
